financials.metric: Revenue and cash-runway inputs (revenue / liquidity / operating cash outflow / net loss)
financials.value: GAAP revenue US$0 — the Condensed Consolidated Statements of Operations contain no revenue line at all and open directly at 'Operating expenses'; the filing states 'As of June 30, 2026, the Company had not derived revenue from its principal business activities' and MD&A calls it 'a development-stage company with no revenue to date'. Cash and cash equivalents US$132.872m + marketable securities US$726.130m = US$859.002m (MD&A: 'approximately $859.0 million'). Net cash used in operating activities US$116.259m for the six months ended 2026-06-30 (H1 2025: US$122.589m). Net loss H1 2026 US$199.039m (Q2 alone US$98.240m; H1 2025 US$229.121m). H1 2026 capex US$14.598m.
financials.unit: US$ (financial-statement amounts filed in US$ thousands)
financials.period: three and six months ended 2026-06-30 (fiscal year = calendar year, no FY/CY mismatch)
financials.source_name: QuantumScape Corporation, Form 10-Q for the quarterly period ended June 30, 2026 (SEC EDGAR)
financials.caveat: Zero revenue under US accounting rules: the income statement has no revenue line at all. The customer billings QuantumScape reports alongside it are not revenue and the company says so.
financials.curator_notes: Publish as 'US$0 GAAP revenue', not a bare 'US$0', and footnote the two non-revenue cash items a critic will point at: non-GAAP customer billings of US$21.8m in H1 2026 (US$11.0m Q1, US$10.8m Q2), which QS itself calls an operational metric and not a GAAP revenue measure; and a US$130m pre-paid initial PowerCo royalty carried as a liability subject to clawback. Do not write '100% of revenue is solid-state' — a share on a zero base says nothing; say 'one operating segment, solid-state lithium-metal, zero revenue'. Any runway figure (about 3.3 to 3.7 years on twice the H1 burn) is our arithmetic, not a company statement: it ignores capital spending and the milestone-contingent PowerCo inflow. Across all 271 us-gaap tags QS has ever filed there is no revenue concept at all. Reader-friendly permalink: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1811414/000119312526316073/0001193125-26-316073-index.htm

financials.metric: Revenue and cash-runway inputs (revenue and grant income / liquidity / operating cash outflow)
financials.value: Total revenue and grant income US$2.805m for H1 2026 (revenue US$1.088m + grant income US$1.717m). Q2 2026 alone was NEGATIVE US$0.268m (revenue −US$1.017m + grant income US$0.749m), driven by a US$1.2m reversal of previously recognised non-government revenue under the SK On R&D licence (change in the constraint on variable consideration). Total liquidity US$419.326m = cash and cash equivalents US$24.284m + available-for-sale securities US$395.042m. Net cash used in operating activities US$27.173m for H1 2026 (H1 2025: US$40.734m). No debt.
financials.unit: US$ (financial-statement amounts filed in US$ thousands)
financials.period: three and six months ended 2026-06-30 (fiscal year end 12-31, so H1 2026 = calendar H1 2026)
financials.source_name: Solid Power, Inc., Form 10-Q for the quarterly period ended June 30, 2026 (SEC EDGAR)
financials.caveat: None of this is product revenue: it is collaboration money from SK On plus US government grants, and the second quarter of 2026 was negative after a US$1.2m reversal.
financials.curator_notes: Do not label this 'revenue attributable to solid-state products'. The filing states the company is 'a research and development company with no commercial operations'. Two mechanical traps: (1) 'Total liquidity US$419.326m' is a company-defined MD&A measure, not a balance-sheet line — the US$395.042m available-for-sale figure is current marketable securities US$218.151m plus long-term AFS bonds US$176.891m, and an automated read of the same filing produced a wrong US$242.4m by taking only the current line. (2) The negative second quarter makes any single-quarter revenue multiple meaningless; use H1 or TTM. A roughly seven-year runway is our arithmetic, not a company statement; the company says liquidity is sufficient for 'at least the next 12 months'. The 2026 equity offering with net proceeds of US$121.3m is researcher-noted and was never confirmed — re-verify before publishing it. Filing date confirmed from the in-document signature block ('Date: August 5, 2026'); the cover-page 'as of August 3, 2026' is the share-count date.

open_gaps: A defensible "solid-state market share" cannot be computed today — not approximately, not with caveats. There is no numerator: QuantumScape has US$0 revenue and has never disclosed a GWh or a cell count; Solid Power's entire revenue line is SK On collaboration money plus DOE grants and went negative in Q2 2026; ProLogium publishes only a cumulative cell count that is a floor first measured at H1 2025. The pool's revenue share is a share of battery revenue, not of solid-state.

No research house in this sweep sizes the solid-state segment at all. There is no analogue to the LightCounting / Cignal / Dell'Oro coverage that exists for optical — no free release giving solid-state market size, growth or vendor ranking. That absence, not a missing number, is the structural gap.

ProLogium's true cumulative shipments as of 2026-09-16 are unknown. Only the >2.4 million floor, first published for H1 2025 and restated unchanged on 2026-09-02, is public, and the company has been running a Giga-level platform since 2024.

ProLogium's own two 2026 releases do not agree on the Dunkirk first phase. The February groundbreaking release stages it 0.8 GWh in 2028, 4 GWh in 2030 and 12 GWh in 2032; the September release says "upon completion of the first phase, the facility is designed to reach 4.0 GWh of annual production capacity" with no year. Both are recorded; neither is reconciled by the company.
No cash or runway data for SES AI, Ilika or Microvast reached this sweep, so no pool verdict can honestly be issued for those three.

No semi-solid shipment figure of any kind has been sourced — not for WeLion, Ganfeng, Farasis or the NIO 150 kWh pack. Ganfeng's Xinyu capacity is recorded, but capacity is not shipment, and the semi-solid leg of the page still has no volume behind it.

The largest names have announced a date and no capacity. CATL restates a 2027 small-batch target with no GWh attached; Samsung SDI said on 2026-07-30 that mass production starts at Ulsan in the second half of 2027 and published no GWh figure with it; Honda's demonstration line in Sakura City (2024-11-21) is given as a floor area of about 27,400 m² and no capacity; Nissan's own release on the Yokohama pilot line carries no capacity at all, and the widely repeated 100 MWh a year from fiscal 2028 is media-attributed. None of them is recorded here.

No listed company has published a built, funded, all-solid-state capacity figure above 0.2 GWh. The largest recorded here is Gotion's 0.2 GWh pilot line; everything larger is either semi-solid (Gotion's 12 GWh quasi-solid line, Ganfeng's 2 GWh at Xinyu), unbuilt (ProLogium's Dunkirk staging), a licence ceiling (QuantumScape and PowerCo), or a material rather than a cell (Solid Power's electrolyte tonnage).

Gotion's 2 GWh all-solid-state mass-production line — design reported complete on 2026-03-02 — has no citable primary source. It was stated on the SZSE investor-interaction platform, which serves an empty JavaScript shell to every deep-link format tried, and the only readable carriers are aggregators. It is deliberately not recorded.

The Chinese pilot lines announced through investor-interaction platforms are outside this file for the same reason: Sunwoda's 0.2 GWh polymer line, Farasis's 0.2 GWh sulfide pilot line and the SAIC / QingTao 0.5 GWh first phase are all sourced only to aggregator re-reports of platform answers or conference remarks. They should be added when the companies state them in a filing or a newsroom release.

CATL's primary record (深交所互动易) has no citable deep link: every deep-link format returns an empty JavaScript shell. The primary can be named and dated but not linked; only the aggregator copy is clickable.

The two researchers gave conflicting QuantumScape FY2026 capital-expenditure guidance — US$40–60m in one record against about US$27–37m in the other — and neither was resolved. No QS capex figure is published until it is re-pulled from the shareholder letter or the 10-Q.
Solid Power's 2026 equity offering net proceeds of US$121.3m come from researcher notes only and were never confirmed against the filing.

SNE Research does not give per-company shares for CALB, Gotion, EVE, SVOLT or REPT in its free release text — only GWh and year-on-year growth. The widely circulated percentages for those five originate from CnEVPost reading SNE's chart image and are not verifiable in the SNE body.

Segment revenue is recorded for Panasonic only. BYD reports batteries bundled inside its automotive segment and cannot be split (evidence in segment_disclosure). Samsung SDI, TDK, Murata and Maxell all publish a battery or energy segment, but no figure has been read off a filing for them yet, so they stay out of the computed pool — and the reason the page gives for their exclusion is a placeholder, not a finding about their disclosure.

Nobody discloses solid-state revenue. Every segment figure in this file is a battery or energy segment standing in for a track whose revenue is still approximately zero, which is why the page shows shipments and capacity instead of a share chart.
The rejected-items list was not visible in the original sweep, so this file cannot report what failed adversarial verification or why.

The original sweep was dominated by optical entries (roughly 20 of 27 confirmed items), so the solid-state track was researched far more thinly than the optical one and should not be treated as an equally complete pass. The capacity rows here were collected separately on 2026-09-16.
citability_verdict: Four source types are safe to cite on a public page, in descending order of strength. (1) SEC filings on EDGAR — QuantumScape's and Solid Power's 10-Qs are primary, permanent, signed under liability, and are the only documents here where anything is legally attested; cite the Archives permalink (or the lighter filing-index URL) and take the filing date from the in-document signature block, never from a search snippet. (2) First-party company releases on the company's own newsroom or its paid wire (ProLogium via prologium.com / GlobeNewswire) — citable and date-confirmable from the in-body dateline, but you must check whether the number is a fresh measurement or recycled boilerplate: ProLogium's ">2.4 million cells" was first announced in July 2025 and merely restated unchanged fourteen months later. (3) Free press releases from a named research house where the number sits in the free body, not behind the report paywall (SNE Research) — citable with the house name plus the exact release date, preferring SNE's English-edition URL; the underlying Monthly Tracker is sold, but the headline table is not. (4) Chinese trade aggregators (OFweek) as a readable secondary only — attribute the primary event (CATL's SZSE 互动易 answer of 2026-09-09) and use the aggregator as the clickable link, because 互动易 is a JavaScript single-page app with no working deep link; take the date from the page's own byline block, since Chinese pages' search-engine dates are unreliable. Not safe to cite: paywalled bodies (Caixin's Davos report — headline and lede only were readable); capacity numbers that appear in media but not in the company release (ProLogium's 0.5 GWh/yr Taoyuan line, the Dunkirk staging); per-company shares read off a chart image by a re-reporter (CnEVPost's figures for CALB, Gotion, EVE, SVOLT, REPT); non-GAAP "customer billings" presented as revenue; and any licence ceiling (QS/PowerCo's 85 GWh) presented as capacity.

readiness.source_name: 每日经济新闻 (National Business Daily), 「2026夏季达沃斯论坛｜宁德时代创始人曾毓群：技术路线成熟后，需经历产品化、商品化阶段，才能判断是扩大产能还是等待下一代技术」 (记者 张宏)

readiness.curator_notes: Re-sourced on 2026-09-16. The row previously cited an OFweek article that says only 「只给全固态电池的技术成熟度打了4分」 — a score of 4 with no denominator anywhere on the page — while the row asserted 'level 4 of 9' and a unit of 'TRL score (x of 9)'. The denominator is real but it is not on that page: 每日经济新闻 quotes 曾毓群 giving the 1-to-9 scale in the same sentence as the 4, and 新浪财经 (https://finance.sina.com.cn/tech/discovery/2026-06-24/doc-inienxzw6245046.shtml, 2026-06-24) carries the same quote as 'level1-9 ... 现在只到了level4，level9是可以量产'. Both verified verbatim on 2026-09-16. Attribute the 1-to-9 framing to the speaker, not to the formal TRL standard: the outlet adds the TRL gloss itself (「根据TRL九级技术成熟度体系」), 曾毓群 says 技术成熟度从1级到9级. This statement and CATL's 2026-09-09 investor-platform answer are separate events — different speaker context, date and venue — and must not be merged into one data point; the 互动易 reply contains no maturity rating at all. Caixin's fuller report (https://international.caixin.com/2026-06-25/102457176.html) is paywalled and was not used.
